text:
anya: Heads-up — saw a small but consistent quality regression on Mixtral-8k after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. eval-run regression ~0.9% BLEU-ish on our summarization suite.
sam: ugh, observed that too on staging canary. latency improved but decode outputs diverge slightly. stack traces point to attention kernel swap for attn dims >= 128. :thinking_face:
luis: repro steps? i ran perf harness with 4k and 8k sequences, toggled selector flag. 8k picks tiled-attn-v2 now, previously used native-attn.
maria: repro logs (short):
```
# selector decision for mixtral-8k
seq=8192 heads=16 head_dim=128 -> kernel=tiled-attn-v2 (lat 82ms)
seq=8192 heads=16 head_dim=128 -> kernel=native-attn (lat 110ms)  # pre-change
BLEU_drop=0.9% on sum-suite
```
sam: interesting — tiled-attn-v2 uses a slightly different RoPE interpolation path to pack tiles, which can shift floating rounding and kv cache indexing. could be a numeric drift.
anya: we saw similar drift last year when quant fast-path picked int8-fast with fused softmax -> tiny prob shifts, but used to be benign. here it's larger. maybe compounded with RoPE scaling change in mixtral config PR #4721.
luis: i profiled the runtime: perf-bot uploaded flamegraphs and TVM kernel traces: https://artifacts.redwood/dumps/1767654321/fg.html
perf-bot: perf artifact available: s3://redwood-artifacts/perf/1767654321/mixtral-canary.tar.gz
maria: can we isolate whether it's kernel swap vs RoPE scaling? quick A/B: revert selector only (force native-attn) and run eval, then force tiled-attn but revert the RoPE scale from PR #4721 and run eval.
sam: started A/B now on canary (2 nodes): a) force-native b) force-tiled + old-rope. ETA ~12m.
anya: also log KV cache behavior: noticed minor mismatch in kv-cache hit counters during streaming replays — could be stale prefix eviction timing. luis, did selector change touch KV placement?
luis: selector change is pure kernel routing; but tiled-attn-v2 keeps KV shards per-tile which nudges our cache TTL heuristics — we might be evicting earlier because per-tile footprints look larger.
maria: results: A) force-native -> BLEU back to baseline, latency regressions +28ms, B) force-tiled + old-rope -> BLEU back to baseline and latency still good. so root cause is RoPE scaling mismatch interacting with tiled-attn path.
sam: aha. so the tiled path expects RoPE pre-scaling that PR changed for long-context stabilization. that pre-scaling alters phase factors, causing token misalignment on certain prompts.
anya: decision? rollback PR #4721 or adjust tiled-attn to apply compatible RoPE transform?
luis: patch idea: add a compatibility shim in tiled-attn to detect legacy-rope flag per-model-version and apply the old-phase math when model pinned to older weights. small performance hit but keeps correctness. PR ready: #4756.
maria: canary deploy of #4756?
deploy-bot: canary deploy of PR #4756 started to eng-runtime-canary-cluster.
perf-bot: quick perf summary after canary rollout: tiled-attn w/compat shim: median latency 84ms (vs 82ms before), p95 140ms. quality delta: BLEU within 0.05% of baseline.
sam: thumbs up — acceptable tradeoff. We should also add a selector heuristic: prefer native-attn for head_dim==64 or if model has legacy-rope flag set. luis can you add rule?
luis: yup will add a small rule table and unit tests. also adding an invariant test in runtime-evals that runs small sample prompts across selector permutations to catch this earlier.
anya: follow-ups: (1) deconflict RoPE change in model-offline PR (owner @maria) (2) add selector/rope compatibility matrix in runtime configs (3) add canary gate that runs eval-suite before promoting. I'll file tickets.
maria: filed: RW-3312 (compat shim rollout), RW-3313 (selector heuristics), RW-3314 (canary eval gate).
sam: big lesson: kernel swaps can be performant but interact in surprising ways with model pre-processing. we should add a short doc in eng-runtime on "kernel compatibility hazards".
anya: thanks all, merging #4756 after canary stays green for 24h. :thumbsup:
